referent.take: Trust-first tone: plain confident language, transparency as a selling point, numeric/money content treated as the hero element, restrained UI chrome, no gimmicks competing with the balance/amount display, security and clarity foregrounded over playfulness
referent.leave: Marketing-site layout patterns (long scroll, country list, testimonial carousel) do not apply to an app shell; we are extracting tone/trust-signal language, not literal layout

style.name: Swiss / International — grid-based, sans-serif, mathematical alignment

note: Design tokens (colors, typography scale, spacing, radii, shadows, motion) are fully pre-specified by the user in the task prompt with exact hex/px values and are used verbatim, not re-derived from the referent. Swiss/International style governs LAYOUT DISCIPLINE on top of those fixed tokens: strict 4px spacing grid, consistent 20px screen padding, mathematically consistent card/list rhythm, no decorative gradients beyond the one specified --gradient-balance (reserved exclusively for BalanceCard, not reused elsewhere), restrained shadow usage (sm/md/lg only, used sparingly), alignment-driven hierarchy over ornament. This avoids default 'purple gradient everywhere + cards-in-cards' AI convergence by constraining gradient use to a single intentional surface and enforcing grid alignment elsewhere.
